cards: Ammianus Marcellinus was a Greek-born Roman soldier and historian.
Theodosius I was a Roman emperor who died in 395 CE, the last to rule both the eastern and western halves of the empire.
Samudragupta was an emperor of the Gupta Empire who reigned c. 335–375 CE.
Licinius was Roman emperor from 308 to 324.
Ezana was a king of Aksum who reigned c. 325–340 CE.
Kumarajiva was a Buddhist monk and translator from the oasis kingdom of Kucha, the son of an Indian father and a Kuchean princess.
Jerome was a Christian priest, scholar and Doctor of the Church, born in Dalmatia, who spent his later life as a monk in Bethlehem.
Ambrose was bishop of Milan from 374 and one of the four original Doctors of the Latin Church.
Huan Wen was a general and statesman of the Eastern Jin who dominated the court for two decades.
Wang Xizhi was a Chinese calligrapher of the Eastern Jin dynasty, revered as the 'Sage of Calligraphy'.
Ge Hong was a Chinese scholar, alchemist and Daoist writer of the Eastern Jin period from the region south of the Yangtze.
Prudentius (Aurelius Prudentius Clemens) was a Latin Christian poet from Hispania, probably born at Calagurris (Calahorra).
Murong Chui was a Xianbei prince of the Former Yan who won fame as a general but fled to the Former Qin in 369 to escape court intrigue.
Valens was Roman emperor in the east from 364 until his death in 378 CE.
Emperor Yuan of Jin, born Sima Rui, was the founding emperor of the Eastern Jin dynasty.
Fu Jian was the Di ruler of the Former Qin from 357, served by the able minister Wang Meng.
Gildo was a Berber prince, son of Nubel and brother of Firmus, who served Rome as military commander in Africa from 386.
Gregory the Illuminator was the founder and first head of the Armenian Church.
Gu Kaizhi was a Chinese painter of the Eastern Jin dynasty, regarded as one of the founders of Chinese figure painting.
Wang Dao was a Chinese statesman of the Wang clan of Langya who guided the founding of the Eastern Jin dynasty.
Xie An was a Chinese statesman of the Eastern Jin dynasty and head of the aristocratic Xie clan.
Xie Xuan was a Chinese general of the Eastern Jin dynasty and nephew of the statesman Xie An.
Arius was a Christian priest of Alexandria whose teaching that the Son was created by God the Father, and subordinate to him, caused a long controversy in the church.
Chak Tok Ich'aak I was a king of the Maya city of Tikal in the fourth century CE.
Huiyuan (334–416) was a Chinese Buddhist monk of the Eastern Jin period who founded a monastic community on Mount Lu.
Magnentius was a Roman usurper who seized power in the West in January 350 after the murder of Emperor Constans, ruling Gaul, Britain, Spain, Italy and Africa.
Siricius was bishop of Rome from 384 to 399.
Rufinus of Aquileia was a Latin Christian monk, historian and translator who lived for many years in Egypt and Palestine before returning to Italy.
Vadomarius was an Alemannic king of the Brisigavi in the Breisgau in the mid-fourth century.
Zhi Dun was a Buddhist monk and scholar of the Eastern Jin dynasty who moved in the aristocratic circles of Jiankang and the south-east.
Tuoba Gui, posthumously Emperor Daowu, was the founder of the Northern Wei dynasty.
Geunchogo was king of Baekje from 346 to 375, the period of its greatest early power.
Liu Kun was a Western Jin general, poet and governor of Bingzhou in northern China who held out against the Xiongnu state of Han Zhao after the collapse of Jin authority in the north.
Lü Guang was a Di general of Former Qin whom the emperor Fu Jian sent to the Tarim Basin in 382.
Murong De was a Xianbei prince, younger brother of Murong Chui of Later Yan, and founder of Southern Yan.
Saint Nicholas was a 4th-century bishop of Myra in Lycia, in present-day Turkey, venerated across Eastern and Western Christianity as a wonder-worker and patron of sailors and children.
Shi Hu was emperor of the Later Zhao, a state of the Jie people in northern China, from 334 to 349.
Shi Le was a Jie warlord who rose from slavery to become a general of the Han-Zhao state, helping to capture the Jin capital Luoyang in 311.
Synesius was a Greek philosopher from Cyrene, a pupil of Hypatia in Alexandria, who became Bishop of Ptolemais in Cyrenaica around 410.
Wang Meng was the Han Chinese chief minister of Fu Jian, ruler of the Former Qin in northern China.
